blocks.text: Where a loan officer's day actually goes

Public data on this job is thin. No public study measures how loan officers split their time by task. What exists is job data and survey data, and both point the same way. Your day runs on email, documents and software you did not write.

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics describes the work in plain terms. Most firms use underwriting software that generates a loan recommendation. You review that output next to your own assessment. You also collect and verify applicants' financial documents. Then you check loan agreements against federal and state regulations.

O*NET, the occupation database run by the U.S. Department of Labor, adds two signals. Every loan officer in its data answers 'Every day' for email. And 62% say they spend time sitting continually or almost continually. Long stretches at a screen are normal for this job.

The closest thing to a time study here is Microsoft's Work Trend Index. It covers general office workers, though. The average employee spends 57% of time communicating. Email alone is 15%. The heaviest email users, the top 25%, spend 8.8 hours a week on email. Use these numbers as context, not as a picture of your week.
Put the public picture next to your own job. It looks like this:

items: Email with borrowers, processors, underwriters and agents, every day
Collecting and verifying bank statements, pay stubs and other financial documents
Reviewing underwriting software output against your own read of the file
Checking loan agreements against federal and state rules
Sitting at a screen for long stretches between calls and files

blocks.text: Loan officer email on Mac: where most replies start

Email touches every other task. A borrower asks where a document is. A processor asks for a signed form. An underwriter sends a condition. Each message lands in your inbox, and each one needs a reply that is both correct and clear.

Gmail and Outlook both work for this, and the setup differs. The latest listed Outlook for Mac release is 16.114.3, dated Oct 27, 2026. Microsoft says the Office apps need macOS 14 Sonoma or later to keep getting updates. Older Macs still run them, but they stop getting updates. Check your version under Apple menu > About This Mac.

Use Lazur for the draft, not the send. Hold ⌥ ⌘ on the thread and ask what the borrower needs. Then ask for a short reply. Read it before you send it. Check every date, amount and document name. Lazur does not click send for you, so the final step stays with you.

Follow-ups are where email slips. Gmail can snooze a thread until you are ready to act. See [how to snooze an email in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/snooze-an-email-in-gmail). For a reply you want to hold until a set time, read [how to schedule an email in Gmail on Mac](/how-to/schedule-an-email-to-send-later-in-gmail). If your firm uses a team inbox, read [how to add a shared mailbox in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/add-a-shared-mailbox-in-outlook).

Notes are the other half of the job. Hold fn and dictate the file note in plain words. Something like: appraisal ordered, waiting on the report. Lazur types clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Read it again before you save it to the file.
Mistakes that cost the most time in email

items: Letting email set the order of your day. Sort first, then reply.
Accepting a drafted reply that quotes a rate or date you did not check.
Asking Lazur to send mail. It explains and drafts. You send.
Replying to a whole thread when one question needs one answer.

blocks.text: Tell Lazur how you want the draft to sound. Ask for three sentences, a plain tone and no promises about rates or approval. You will edit anyway. A clear brief saves rewrites, and it keeps the draft closer to what your firm allows you to say.
Documents and Excel for loan officers, where the file stalls

Document work stalls because it waits on other people. The file stops until the pay stub arrives. Then you check that names match, dates line up and figures agree with the application. Small mismatches cause most of the rework.

Spreadsheets fill the gaps. Many loan officers keep a sheet for pipeline status, payment comparisons and follow-ups. Excel has a payment function called PMT. It needs a rate for each payment period, a number of payments and a loan amount. The same mistakes show up again and again.

The first mistake is mixing an annual rate with a monthly one. PMT expects the rate for each payment period. The second is entering a percent in a cell that expects a decimal, or the reverse. A formula can look right and still return the wrong payment.

Ask before you type. Hold ⌥ ⌘ on the formula bar and ask what the cell is doing. Lazur reads the formula out loud and names each input. Ask where the rate cell is, and it draws a circle and a label around it on screen.

Lazur explains and points. It does not type the formula, change the cell or check the number against your source. You own the number. Compare it with the rate sheet or the lender's disclosure before a borrower sees it.
For the full sheet setup, read [Excel for mortgage loan officers on Mac](/for/mortgage-loan-officers/excel). It covers pipeline sheets and payment cells in more depth.
Underwriting software: use Lazur to read, not to decide

Underwriting setups differ from firm to firm. BLS says most firms use underwriting software that generates a loan recommendation, and officers review it alongside their own assessment. BLS also says some small banks and credit unions have officers complete underwriting without software. Your setup changes how you use any assistant.

Most loan officers live in a loan origination system all day. ICE's Encompass is one such system. The Encompass LO listing on the App Store is for an iPhone app. It says it requires macOS 15.0 or later and a Mac with an Apple M1 chip or later. It is also marked 'Not verified for macOS.' Treat that as a warning, and ask IT before you assume it runs well on your Mac.

ICE's web developer guide lists Chrome, Safari, Edge and Firefox as supported browsers. It does not name a Mac requirement. ICE's Developer Connect 26.2 release note says to clear the browser cache after major releases. Ask your IT team which browser and version your firm supports.

Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Encompass or any other app. It has no partnership with ICE or any app maker. It sees what is on screen while you hold the shortcut. Ask what a status means and it explains. Ask where a field sits and it points. You still enter every value.
Compliance checks and borrower data

Compliance checks are part of the job. BLS says officers check loan agreements against federal and state regulations. Lazur can explain a clause you paste or show on screen. It cannot tell you what your state requires today. Check the rule itself, and confirm with your compliance team.

Borrower data is the bigger risk. A loan file holds identity numbers, income, account details and addresses. Your employer sets the rules for that data. Follow them. Ask your compliance team whether a voice assistant may see loan screens at all.

Here is what Lazur does with what it sees. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Those are product facts. They are not a policy for your firm.

blocks.text: Do not hold ⌥ ⌘ over a screen with full identity numbers unless your employer's policy allows it. This page makes no compliance certification claim for Lazur. Ask your compliance team first.
Setting up Lazur for loan work on your Mac

Lazur runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Download it from the [download page](/download). Open it once and approve the permissions macOS asks for. Lazur needs to hear you and see the screen when you hold a key, so those permissions matter.

The shortcuts do most of the work. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Hold fn to dictate clean text at the cursor in any app. Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans.

blocks.text: A realistic day and what you say to Lazur

The day below is one plausible pattern. Your mix of email, documents and screens will look different. The point is the handoff. You say a short request. Lazur answers, points or drafts. You make the call on every number and every send.
Notice what Lazur does not do in that day. It does not enter the rate, change the file status or send a reply. Those steps stay with you. In a regulated job, that is where they belong.
Edge cases and mistakes with voice assistants

Edge cases come up on busy days. A borrower may send a scan that is hard to read. A screen may show two files at once. A shared mailbox may hold mail for a team, not for you. In each case, slow down. Ask Lazur what is on screen, then check the source yourself.

blocks.text: Where to go next

Start with one repeating task, not the whole day. Email replies make a good first test. Excel payment cells come next. Once those feel safe, move to underwriting screens, and only after your compliance team agrees. Current plans and trial terms are on the [pricing page](/pricing).
Lazur is for the moments when you need a fact, a draft or a step, and you do not want to stop your work to hunt for it. It does not replace your judgment or your employer's rules.

faq.question: Is Lazur an AI assistant for loan officers that works inside my loan system?
faq.answer: Lazur works in any app on your Mac. It sees the screen while you hold ⌥ ⌘, and it answers out loud. It does not operate your loan system for you. It has no partnership with ICE or any app maker.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons or fill in forms?
faq.answer: No. Lazur explains, points and guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click. You do the clicking and the typing.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur on an Intel Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Check your macOS version against the requirements of any loan software you use, because those can differ.

faq.question: Is it safe to use Lazur with borrower data?
faq.answer: Follow your employer's rules on borrower data first. Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and screenshots go to AI providers to answer and are not stored. This page makes no compliance certification claim. Ask your compliance team before you use it on borrower files.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with ICE Encompass?
faq.answer: Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with ICE. It can explain or point at what is on your screen while you hold the shortcut. Check the ICE browser and Mac requirements with your IT team.

faq.question: Does Microsoft's data show how much time loan officers spend on email?
faq.answer: No. Microsoft's Work Trend Index covers general office workers, not loan officers. O*NET reports how often loan officers do email work. It does not report the share of their time.

faq.question: What do I need to start using Lazur for loan work?
faq.answer: You need a Mac on macOS, on Apple silicon or Intel, and the Lazur download. For Outlook for Mac updates, Microsoft requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Current plans and trial terms are on the pricing page.

faq.question: Is dictation included, and where does the text go?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans. Read every dictated note before you save it to a borrower file.
